analysis:
All seven units are documentation-only: inference.md (a date bump and one new failure-mode row at line 2555 on add-on hold load fencing), a new docs/architecture/security/local-control.md, and docs/developer/test.md (test filters and coverage table). No executable code changed, so there are no direct security regressions.

The new local-control.md describes the add-on hold socket and lifecycle mailbox (A-018, TB-012, T-059). Its stated controls are: kernel audit-token peer verification at accept and again per request, a bounded and timed request line, a mailbox request bound to the provider process identity and under one minute old, no-follow and non-blocking owner-only reads of the hold record and mailbox files, and a DEBUG-only dev identity override. It also states that a same-user attacker is outside the boundary, and that the coordinator treats the busy_* fields as self-reported.

The doc cites T-060 repeatedly, but T-060 is not in the supplied definition index (the index runs to T-059). The canonical threat model may not define T-060 yet. That is a documentation and threat-model drift item for the platform side, not a finding, because the threat-model YAML was not in this batch.

The doc says an unreadable hold record fails open and the provider starts unheld. That is a stated design choice. It is only relevant to availability, and it is a same-user capability.

The doc says every build honors DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET. The doc relies on the LaunchAgent not passing it, and I could not verify that. The AddonIPCServer, AddonPeerPolicy, AddonHoldStore and LifecycleMailbox implementations were not supplied, so every claim above is unverified against source. The next pass should check that the code matches the doc, in particular accept-time verification before a slot is taken and the per-request re-verification.
